sections.content:
Now I see:
- Frame at BELOW (45,25)-(53,38), purple
- Block: 75 purple + 25 white
- The white cells are at (34,32)-(38,36), which is the top-right 5x5 corner
So the block now has:
- Top 5 rows: left 5 columns purple (25 cells), right 5 columns white (25 cells) - wait, that doesn't add up
- Actually: 75 purple + 25 white = 100 total
- White at (34,32)-(38,36) = 5 rows x 5 cols = 25 cells (top-right corner)
- Purple at (34,27)-(43,36) minus the white = 75 cells
So the block has:
- Top-right 5x5: white (25 cells)
- Everything else: purple (75 cells)
This makes sense. Before the stamp, the block had a vertical split (left purple, right white). The stamp from BELOW with purple affected the bottom 5 rows, making them purple. So:
- Top 5 rows: left 5 purple, right 5 white (from the vertical split)
- Bottom 5 rows: all purple (from the stamp)
Result: top-right 25 white, rest 75 purple.
Now I need to stamp the top-right 25 cells with purple to make the entire block purple. But wait, I already tried making the block all purple and it didn't complete the level.
Let me reconsider the goal. The palette has white on top and purple on bottom. I've tried:
1. All white - didn't complete
2. All purple - didn't complete
3. Horizontal split (top white, bottom purple) - haven't achieved this yet
4. Vertical split (left purple, right white) - didn't complete
To create a horizontal split with white on top and purple on bottom:
- Top 5 rows: all white (50 cells)
- Bottom 5 rows: all purple (50 cells)
Currently:
- Top 5 rows: left 5 purple, right 5 white
- Bottom 5 rows: all purple
So I need to stamp the top-left 25 cells with white. To do this, I need to stamp from the ABOVE position with white. The frame is currently at BELOW.
Path from BELOW to ABOVE:
- BELOW --LEFT--> BELOW-LEFT
- BELOW-LEFT --UP--> LEFT
- LEFT --UP--> ABOVE-LEFT
- ABOVE-LEFT --RIGHT--> ABOVE
That's LEFT, UP, UP, RIGHT.
Or: BELOW --LEFT--> BELOW-LEFT --UP--> LEFT --UP--> ABOVE-LEFT --RIGHT--> ABOVE
Wait, from LEFT, UP goes to ABOVE-LEFT. So:
- BELOW --LEFT--> BELOW-LEFT
- BELOW-LEFT --UP--> LEFT
- LEFT --UP--> ABOVE-LEFT
- ABOVE-LEFT --RIGHT--> ABOVE
That's LEFT, UP, UP, RIGHT.
Let me try this.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Frame at BELOW (45,25), purple
# Block: top-right 25 white, rest 75 purple
# Need to stamp top-left with white
# Path from BELOW to ABOVE: LEFT -> UP -> UP -> RIGHT
result = action(['LEFT', 'UP', 'UP', 'RIGHT'])
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
for n in nodes:
    if n['color'] == 'g' and n['pixels'] > 20:
        b = n['boundary']
        min_r, max_r = min(p[0] for p in b), max(p[0] for p in b)
        min_c, max_c = min(p[1] for p in b), max(p[1] for p in b)
        print(f"Frame at ({min_r},{min_c})-({max_r},{max_c})")
        break

# Select white and stamp
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 4, 'col': 37}, 'SPACE'])
print(f"After white stamp from above: done={result.get('done', False)}")

# Check block state
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
for n in nodes:
    if n['color'] in ['W', 'p'] and 20 <= n['pixels'] <= 100:
        b = n['boundary']
        min_r, max_r = min(p[0] for p in b), max(p[0] for p in b)
        min_c, max_c = min(p[1] for p in b), max(p[1] for p in b)
        print(f"  color={n['color']}, pixels={n['pixels']}, bbox=({min_r},{min_c})-({max_r},{max_c})")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
